problem:
In a medical imaging facility, a tracer is found with $25%$ of its original sodium-22 content. Given that the half-life of sodium-22 is $2.6$ years, how old is the tracer? Round your answer to **one decimal place**.

The tracer is approximately
{{field-1}}
years old.
worked_solution:
The mass $M(t)$ of a radioactive substance at time $t$ can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
{M}^{′}(t)=-kM(t),\,M(0)={M}_{0}.
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-kt}.
$$

The half-life ${t}_{1/2}$ is the time taken for the mass of the substance to reduce by one half and is given by

$$
{t}_{1/2}=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}.
$$

Since we know that ${t}_{1/2}=2.6$ years, we have

$$
2.6=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}\,⇒\,k=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2.6}.
$$

So, we have

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/2.6}.
$$

We wish to calculate the time $t$ such that $M(t)=0.25{M}_{0}.$ So, we set up our equation as follows:

$$
0.25{M}_{0}={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/2.6}
$$

Solving this equation for $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}0.25{M}_{0} & ={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/2.6} \\ 0.25\cancel{{M}_{0}} & =\cancel{{M}_{0}}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/2.6} \\ 0.25 & ={e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/2.6} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.25) & =ln\,({e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/2.6}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.25) & =-\frac{t\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2.6} \\ t & =-\frac{2.6\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.25)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ t & ≈5.2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the tracer is approximately $5.2$ years old.
